correctness.rationale: For every n>=3, square-zero maps are exactly initial-one-fiber maps whose entire image lies in that fiber; this yields |S_n|=2^(n-2). Necessity of m>=M+s follows from comparing the two factor images and requiring s distinct intermediates outside the second factor one-fiber. An explicit construction of u and v with u^2=v^2=epsilon proves sufficiency. Output/run binomial enumeration gives b_n and a formal geometric series proves OEIS A005251 generating function. Nilpotency S_n^(n-1)={epsilon} and a nonzero indecomposable whose square is zero prove S_n\S_n^2 uniquely minimally generates. Exhaustive compositions in checker.py n<=11 confirm the equivalence and counts; experiments are not offered as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The complete Korkmaz–Ayık (2021) full text, including Theorem 3.4 and Examples 3.5–3.6, proves only a lower bound for N_2(C_n), an individual nonfactorability example at n=6, and rank=4 at n=5. The exact all-n factorization iff criterion and rank were not established there. The new rank 9 at n=6 exceeds the earlier lower bound 8. Published nilpotency-degree counts and full-nilpotent-semigroup rank do not imply the exact N_2(C_n)^2 image. OEIS already lists the integer sequence and recurrence, which are expressly not claimed novel. Full 2023 dissertation inaccessible; see residual risks.
residual_risks: A 2023 doctoral thesis on similar semigroups was not available in full, and could include an unindexed equivalent exact result.

value.rationale: Addresses the exact minimal generator rank of the natural index-two nilpotent ideal explicitly left at a lower bound by Korkmaz–Ayık (2021), with a uniform necessary-and-sufficient factorization criterion and explicit construction. The exact rank already differs from the published 2^(n-3) bound at n=6, and rank ~2^(n-2) while the decomposable fraction vanishes exponentially. The b_n integer sequence itself is pre-existing and is only an auxiliary count, not the asserted novelty. The result is neither an arbitrary slice nor a routine recomputation of a known table.
